subject: FastRetail: latency probe & hosted vs dedicated next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: FastRetail: latency probe & hosted vs dedicated next steps

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path forward so we can qualify whether Hosted API will meet your needs or if we should move toward a Dedicated capacity trial.

Key signals you gave us on the call:
- Peak traffic: ~500 QPS for product search ranking windows during promotions, sustained baseline ~150 QPS.
- Latency target: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 200 ms for the reranking workflow (typical prompt ~40 tokens, response ~60 tokens).
- Business tolerance: can accept slightly higher cold-start or tail latency for non-critical batches, but core search must meet the 95p SLA.
- Compliance: planning team is okay with shared-hosted if we can agree on data retention & audit hooks; still evaluating VPC for procurement.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) We run a 2-hour comparative benchmark (Hosted API vs small Dedicated pool) using your SLO profile to reproduce the 150/500 QPS pattern and measure 95p latency.
2) We'll provide the test harness and a short matrix of configuration knobs (batching window, concurrency, retry/fallback policy) we intend to try — to be reviewed by your infra lead.
3) You confirm a window for the benchmark and whether we can ingest a small set of anonymized production traces (or use the SLO profile you attach).

Deliverables from Redwood after the run: per-model latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99), token-level cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated, and clear recommendation (hosted = pass / hosted = fails -> Dedicated suggested config).

If that plan sounds good, I can schedule the run next week and loop in our infra engineer.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: fastretail-slo-profile.csv (please attach if available)
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, FastRetail IT <it@fastretail.com>
Date: 2028-09-16T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: latency probe & hosted vs dedicated next steps

Irene — thanks, that summary is perfect. Attaching the SLO profile export (fastretail-slo-profile.csv). A few clarifications inline: 

- Peak is a bit bursty around promotions (500 QPS for ~10-15 minute windows, could spike to 650 QPS if multiple campaigns overlap). Baseline is ~150 QPS.
- 95th latency target is firm at 200 ms for the reranker; p99 can be higher but prefer < 400 ms.
- We prefer Hosted for speed-to-market, but procurement will sign off on Dedicated if Hosted can't meet the 95p consistently.
- Compliance: we need to confirm data retention and ability to turn on redaction. Our security lead asked whether Redwood can provide per-request audit IDs into a customer-owned logging sink — if Hosted can export to our account or a collector, that helps.

We can run the benchmark the week of Sep 25. I'll coordinate a short call with our infra lead (cc'd) to approve the sampling traces.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Platforms, FastRetail
samira.khan@fastretail.com | +1 (617) 555-0188

Attachment: fastretail-slo-profile.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: latency probe & hosted vs dedicated next steps

Looping in a short test plan and what we'll vary during the run. High-level notes:

- Test matrix (attached pilot-matrix.yml) — we will sweep: (1) batching window [0ms, 10ms, 25ms], (2) concurrency per worker [8, 16, 32], (3) KV cache warm vs cold, (4) model variant: base quantized vs fp16.
- Measurement: collect per-request timestamps at client and server, compute p50/p90/p95/p99 for request completion time and token time. We'll also report token-cost and effective QPS achieved.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted starts with our standard autoscaling config; Dedicated uses a small reserved pool (2 nodes) with identical model artifact.

Two asks for FastRetail:
1) Can you share 5 representative prompts (sample-prompts.txt) and average token length? We want to match prompt shape.
2) Confirm that pushing anonymized traces is ok for the sandbox run (we won't store traces beyond the benchmark run).

If both ok, I will provision the test harness and propose Sep 26 09:00-11:00 ET for the run (that's Sep 26 06:00-08:00 PT). If that window doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: pilot-matrix.yml
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fastretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, FastRetail IT <it@fastretail.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: latency probe & hosted vs dedicated next steps

Ben / Irene — good plan. Confirming:

- We'll provide 5 sample prompts and approximate token counts (attached sample-prompts.txt). Average prompt length ~45 tokens; response ~65 tokens.
- Anonymized traces: IT has approved delivering a 30-minute sample trace to the sandbox S3 bucket you provide; they asked for a one-time presigned URL approach.
- Sep 26 09:00-11:00 ET works for us. Our infra lead (it@fastretail.com) will be on the call.
- Regarding audit/export: Hosted is fine if you can push per-request audit IDs to our collector (we will share collector endpoint and auth). If not feasible we'll evaluate Dedicated on the results.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Samira
